chapter: Les Hite, Sebastian's and Duke Ellington
title: Duke's invitation to rejoin and the money problem
summary: Ellington wanted Royal back in 1931-32 but paid too little to leave Los Angeles; Lawrence Brown joined to pay for his Cadillac.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Well, had joining while he was here. Did he talk to you about (inaudible)?

Oh, yes, he -- oh, he talked about me going back there in -- way back, '31, '32. So, that was supposed to be a set thing that was going to happen. But he wasn't offering much money anyway for a guy to be out on the road. In those days, if you was paying a guy a hundred dollars a week or $125 a week, the orchestra leader felt as though he was giving you a whole lot of money. That wasn't no good for me, because I was doing almost that well at home in those days and didn't have to worry about no room rent or no food and I was doing all right. So, I wasn't worrying about going to New York, living in those tenements.
Well, you said, at the time that Duke Lawrence joined Duke had that (inaudible) talked to you about joining him, too, is that right?
That's around the same time. That was around the same time, when he --
But You had talked money with him?
I don't know what he talked. Lawrence had to pay --
Lawrence had to pay for that 16-cylinder Cadillac. That's why he went, to make a few extra dollars to pay for the 16-cylinder Cadillac that he had out there that he was trying to pay for.
